fills.agents:
- main: The owner's assistant in chat and Telegram.
- scout: The only agent that reads the web; research behind the research tool.
- curator: Keeps the vault wiki and long-term memory tidy.
- mission: Carries out the owner's tasks, once or repeating (research, briefings, shopping, cleanup analyses).
- desk: Writes the Topic Desk briefings.
- builder: Codes the owner's approved changes in the sandbox.
- planner: Splits an approved idea into tasks with dependencies, so parallel builders can take them.
- opencode: The spare coding agent and the code map's enrichment.
- doctor: The Health doctor; turns open health issues into findings and fixes.
- editor: The Editor; sorts the stack's open ideas so the owner sees few, coherent change requests.
- maintainability: The weekly maintainability review of recently changed code.
- self-review: The weekly self-review; turns the stack's signals into improvement ideas.
- intake: Turns a task given in one sentence into its specification and plan, and hands it to the door that does that work.
- memory: The Memory Keeper; looks after every memory store, fixes its faults within its rules and keeps each change undoable (docs/MEMORY.md).
- inbox: The Inbox digest; hands newsletters on a watched topic to that topic, files others worth keeping into the vault.
- postmaster: Looks after the owner's Gmail, carefully. Files the stack's own mail under its label and watches the copy on the NAS.
- scribe: The one writer of every repository's wiki. Seeds it at onboarding, finds how a repository is built and tested, and folds what each change learned into it.
- reviewer: Reviews a whole change through three lenses (requirements, security, this repository's conventions) on the other engine than the code's.
- prober: Tries a change for real in the sandbox (starts it, calls it, drives its pages) and keeps the evidence.
- coach: Turns the agents' scorecards into agent changes, each replayed on the agent's past runs before it may ship.
- analyst: Turns a specification or documentation into numbered, testable requirements with their sources; reads specs, never code.
- tester: Writes acceptance tests from the requirements alone, before or beside the code, each test named after its requirement.
- breaker: Tries to make the software fail (edge cases, property-based tests, odd inputs) and leaves each failure as a reproducing test.
- tracer: Maps each requirement to the code and tests that fulfil it, with file and line evidence, and names the ones not met.
- judge: Runs every test of the task's repository in the sandbox and sends failures back to the step that must fix them.
- presenter: Writes the owner's report of a task from what every step did, the tests and the trace, plainly and with evidence.
fills.name: bug-fix
fills.text: When a bug is reported, an analyst reads it and decides whether it is a real bug or a question. A question gets answered. A real bug is reproduced, fixed by the builder, the tests run, and a judge checks the result and sends it back to the fix if tests fail. I approve before the fix is posted on the ticket.

fills.name: weekly-review
fills.text: Every week, collect what changed in my repositories, summarise it, and send me a short review.

fills.name: supplier-check
fills.text: For each supplier on the list, research their latest news and prices, then compare them and tell me which one to pick.
